Finally, a recent systematic review and meta-analysis, including the results of 14 studies and 189,966 participants ranging
between 10 and 64 years, reported the association between UPF with overweight and obesity (Askari et al., 2020). In sensitivity
analysis, higher UPF intake was associated with an increase risk of 33% (pooled effect size: 1.33; 95% CI:1.18, 1.49, p < 0.001)
of being overweight and 73% (pooled effect size: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.36, 2.20, p < 0.001) of obesity. Thus, both clinical and epidemi-
ological studies implicate UPF intake with a higher risk of developing obesity.
Cardiovascular and metabolic diseases
With regards to metabolic diseases, a population-based cohort study in France (NutriNet-Santé) longitudinally evaluated the effect
of ultra-processed foods consumption of more than 100,000 French adults. Over a ﬁve-year period, a 10% increase in the consump-
